body.x: FakeEyes Co., Ltd. (CEO Mason Kim) participated on Friday, December 12, in the “Global Media Meetup” hosted by AVING News’ International Press Club (IPC) for domestic companies and startups.

The Global Media Meetup focuses on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aims to proactively report on CES 2026 Innovation Award winners and CES-participating startups through global media channels and expand business opportunities.

FakeEyes is a Korean company that has developed technological expertise in vision AI and extended reality (XR). Based on this combined capability, the company has introduced AI-based live-fire sniper training systems and XR-based close-combat training platforms, proposing new standards for future combat training.

Its live-fire sniper training system has been officially adopted as a training program by the Republic of Korea Special Warfare Command, contributing to the cultivation of advanced snipers. The related technologies are protected by international patents (PCT), and their potential for global expansion has received high evaluation. Through continued expansion and advancement of its defense-focused technology platforms, FakeEyes aims to keep contributing to the development of intelligent professional forces and the enhancement of combat capabilities.

At CES 2026, FakeEyes plans to unveil a walking assistance device and navigation platform for the visually impaired, developed through a three-company consortium with SimSimi Inc. and DIVE XR, leveraging its proven vision AI capabilities.

The platform is designed to support independent and safe mobility for people with visual impairments. It consists of a wearable device equipped with a camera and speaker, along with a mobile application.

body.cap: FakeEyes CEO Mason Kim conducts interviews with journalists from five countries—the United States, France, the United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, and Vietnam. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: A single camera mounted on the device applies a monocular depth estimation (MDF) engine to acquire wide-ranging three-dimensional information about the surrounding environment, while also incorporating semantic segmentation technology that classifies objects in real-time video and image data at the pixel level.

FakeEyes integrated these engines into an ultra-lightweight on-device AI system, enabling rapid guidance on user-defined routes and potential hazards scattered throughout walking environments. Because the system does not require network connectivity, it delivers consistent service quality even in areas with poor mobile network coverage.
CEO Mason Kim explained, “Our assistive device for the visually impaired offers strong cost competitiveness in both manufacturing and usage, while also featuring ultra-low power consumption.”

He added, “The platform recognizes hazardous situations and objects along walking routes, infers their movement direction and distance, and supports voice guidance and walking function control through voice recognition technology. With this highly efficient platform that integrates diverse functions, we aim to expand not only into the domestic market but also into barrier-free solution markets overseas.”

Meanwhile, AVING News has introduced Korean companies to the world through partnership cooperation with more than 800 media outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building on its long-established global media network, AVING News launched the International Press Club in August. Media outlets participating in this Global Media Meetup included Innovation & Tech Today from the United States, Le Café Du Geek from France, Arageek from the United Arab Emirates, and Digitimes from Taiwan.
